problem_statement: The sys_heap allocator must support a configurable runtime hardening level. At the 'full' level, every allocation must carry an 8-byte canary trailer, computed from the chunk address and size, that is validated when the memory is freed (and poisoned afterward to catch double-frees); a corrupted canary on free must be detected and treated as fatal. The heap's minimum-size constants (Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE / Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR) must be computed at build time from the actual chunk struct layout (including the canary trailer) rather than from hardcoded magic numbers, so a single-byte allocation from a Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE-sized heap succeeds and Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR(n) is large enough to allocate n bytes. The existing alloc/free/realloc/validate behaviour must remain correct under these settings.

verification.reason: The hidden tests use the macro CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE and the Kconfig options CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL / CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_NONE by exact name, but the problem statement never provides these names, so an agent could not produce code that the tests compile and pass against.

problems.detail: The heap_align test uses the macro CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE (multiplied by CHUNK_UNIT to get the trailer size in bytes). The statement mentions an '8-byte canary trailer' but never gives the name CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE or states that it expresses the trailer size in chunk units (1 when canaries are enabled, 0 otherwise).

The testcase.yaml files enable CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL=y and CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_NONE=y as extra_configs. The statement references the 'full' level in prose but never gives the exact Kconfig option names CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL or CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_NONE.

problem_statement_fixed: The sys_heap allocator must support a configurable runtime hardening level, selected via the Kconfig choice SYS_HEAP_HARDENING with at least the options CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_NONE and CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL (among others). At the 'full' level (CONFIG_SYS_HEAP_HARDENING_FULL=y), every allocation must carry an 8-byte canary trailer, computed from the chunk address and size, that is validated when the memory is freed (and poisoned afterward to catch double-frees); a corrupted canary on free must be detected and treated as fatal. The trailer size expressed in chunk units (i.e. the number of CHUNK_UNIT-sized units the trailer occupies) must be available to callers as the macro CHUNK_TRAILER_SIZE, which is 1 when canaries are enabled and 0 otherwise, so that code can account for the trailer when computing allocation extents. The heap's minimum-size constants (Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE / Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR) must be computed at build time from the actual chunk struct layout (including the canary trailer) rather than from hardcoded magic numbers, so a single-byte allocation from a Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE-sized heap succeeds and Z_HEAP_MIN_SIZE_FOR(n) is large enough to allocate n bytes. The existing alloc/free/realloc/validate behaviour must remain correct under these settings.
